The world

Marketing Dive · 3 Sep 2026

PepsiCo hands global media to Publicis, ending a 20 year run with OMD

PepsiCo moved its global media business from Omnicom to Publicis Groupe, which will build a new AI and data driven "One PepsiCo" model spanning strategy, planning, activation, connected identity and technology across more than 200 markets and brands, including Pepsi, Gatorade and Lay's. Omnicom keeps creative, sports marketing and PR work, and Publicis is withdrawing from the pitch for Coca-Cola's global media account to focus on the new relationship.

Why it mattersThis is the second Coca-Cola-scale account Publicis has pulled from Omnicom's orbit in two years, after taking Coke's North American media business from WPP in 2025. A network that consolidates strategy, data and activation into one owned model is out-competing the traditional media-plus-creative agency split.
Digiday · 3 Sep 2026

Ace Hardware adds weather triggered programmatic ads to its retail media network

RedVest Media, Ace Hardware's retail media arm, is nearly a year old. Its newest feature switches a campaign's messaging automatically based on real time conditions such as rainfall, snowfall, air clarity or the EV index, useful for a co-op that sells power tools, snow equipment and grass seed. The update also brings incrementality measurement with control groups, an Influential and Publicis backed influencer program, a DoorDash ad partnership (91% of DoorDash Ace shoppers have never visited a physical store) and a Pacvue integration.

Why it mattersAce's business has always moved with the weather. What changes is that the ad now moves with it automatically, in the time it takes a storm system to arrive, not the time it takes a media buyer to notice one.
TechCrunch · 8 Aug 2026, effective 7 Sep 2026

X retires Creator Revenue Sharing today for a stricter Original Content Rewards program

X stopped accepting new enrollments into Creator Revenue Sharing on 7 August and retires the program today, 7 September. Two final payouts landed 14 and 28 August, and the last one, covering earnings through today, arrives around 11 September. From 8 September, eligible creators (X Premium, 500 verified followers, 500,000 verified impressions) can apply for Original Content Rewards, which pays only on qualified impressions from Premium users on original posts and excludes reposts and lightly repackaged content.

Why it mattersThe old program rewarded reposting and engagement farming as much as making anything. Paying only for verified original work is X admitting its own incentive structure created the low effort feed it now has to fix.
Digiday · 2 Sep 2026

Brands turn to creators over 30 for an authenticity AI cannot fake

A WordPress VIP survey finds 60% of US consumers call AI in brand messaging a turnoff, while Emarketer data shows 34% of social users are more likely to buy based on an authentic creator review. Brands including Similac are building campaigns around creators like Alex and Jon (10 million plus followers, parenting content) and Ellie Fletcher (36,000 TikTok followers, 3.5 million likes, endometriosis and infertility content), prized less for reach and more for how their presence "makes you feel," per Lily Comba of Superbloom. Nearly two thirds of Gen Z no longer shop via TikTok Shop, even as 47% of TikTok users aged 25 to 44 buy products discussed on the platform (Edison Research).

Why it mattersAs AI generated brand content becomes cheap and ubiquitous, a visibly older, visibly specific creator becomes a scarcity signal in itself. The premium is not for audience size, it is for proof of a real, aging, non-synthetic person standing behind the message.
Search Engine Journal and others · hearing 26 Aug 2026

A federal judge calls Google's AI Overviews deal with publishers "really unfair"

At a motion to dismiss hearing in Penske Media Corporation v Google LLC (filed September 2025), Judge Amit Mehta pressed Google on whether its dominance in Search lets it take publisher content for AI Overviews and, per an attendee's account, said the arrangement "seems really unfair." Penske (Rolling Stone, Variety, Billboard, WWD, Deadline) says Google requires publishers to allow their reporting into AI Overviews or accept being down ranked, and ties AI Overviews to a 58% cut in publisher click through rates and a fall of more than a third in Penske's own affiliate revenue since its 2024 peak.

Why it mattersThis hearing sits outside the usual ten day window of this brief, but the case is still active and the number behind it, a 58% click cut, is the clearest figure yet on what AI Overviews cost the outlets whose reporting they summarize.

Social trends

BroBible, Whiskey Riff · late Aug/early Sep 2026

"Down Goes the Whiskey" turns into a brand-jacked meme

  • Country singer Luke Bryan previewed "Down Goes the Whiskey," built on a simple "blank goes the blank" rhyme structure, ahead of his 18 September album.
  • TikTok decided the formula was too easy to mock: the top comment on his post, "fart goes the butt," out-engaged most reaction videos, and the joke spread to his other posts too.
  • Southwest Airlines replied in character with "zoom goes the plane," riding the meme within days of it forming.
  • Status: hot and still spreading as of early September. No verified total view count found across trackers, flagged as such.
Why it mattersA brand's reply beat a brand's campaign. Southwest spent one line and a sense of timing, not a production budget.
Trend trackers · Sep 2026

"How Could This Day Get Any Better" bait and switch reveal

  • A lone item, usually food, sits on a table; on the audio's punchline the camera pans to reveal a ridiculous abundance of the same item.
  • Format-first, easy to imitate in any niche: this cycle's dominant pattern is short, repeatable comedy premises over polished production.
  • Status: rising, riding the same "format-first comedy" wave as New York Fashion Week (from 15 Sep) and the VMAs (27 Sep) move through the FYP.
Why it mattersThe joke resolves in one cut. No script, no edit, no production, which is exactly why it is spreading faster than anything that needs those three things.

Campaigns & brand moves

Marketing Dive · 3 Sep 2026

Hoka x Strava, "Run Your City"

Hoka and Jellyfish (Brandtech Group) turned New York's five boroughs into a month-long running competition: Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, the Bronx and Staten Island log miles via Strava, and digital OOH screens in Times Square, Tribeca, SoHo and Williamsburg cycle ticker style through weekly miles logged, pace and other stats for each borough. The campaign closes with an October 3 block party and a six-creator program covering the five boroughs, led by Collectively.

Why it mattersThe creative is not designed once and run for a month, it is a live scoreboard rebuilt weekly from real Strava data. Borough versus borough is a rivalry format that turns individual training data into a shared, public stake.
Pambianconews · 3 Sep 2026

Pennyblack's complete rebrand

Pennyblack, the Max Mara Group label founded in 1978 and named after the world's first postage stamp, unveiled a new logo, packaging, digital identity and retail concept, debuting with three store openings this September in Lonato, Casalecchio and Assago. The new stores use textured materials, a warm palette with unexpected color accents, and a layout designed as a fluid sequence of spaces without visual breaks, following a new pennyblack.com site launched at the end of May.

Why it mattersA fashion group rebrand that starts with retail architecture, not a logo reveal, is a bet that the store itself is the primary brand touchpoint again, after a decade of digital-first identity work.
Media Key · Sep 2026

Geox Kids, "Step Into the Beat"

Geox's new global Kids Back to School campaign, by Curiosity Box and Akita Film (both Casta Diva Group), borrows K-pop's visual and musical codes, the aesthetic South Korea exported to Generation Alpha, to sell its new kids' shoe collection on rhythm, color and energy. It runs in Italy, the UK, France, Belgium, Spain, Portugal and Greece.

Why it mattersThe campaign's own key visual carries an "AI generated" watermark, a small, telling detail: a legacy Italian footwear brand is now producing its Back to School creative with the same generative tools its Gen Alpha audience uses to make memes, not hiring a separate production house to imitate the look.

What is working in content

BroBible, Whiskey Riff · Sep 2026

Real-time reply beats scheduled content

Southwest Airlines' one-line "zoom goes the plane" comment, riding the "Down Goes the Whiskey" meme within days of it forming, out-performed anything a planned campaign could have produced in that window.

Why it mattersThis is a comment, not a content calendar line. The brands winning attention right now treat the reply box as a channel with its own production budget of zero and its own audience already primed to laugh.
Industry benchmark data · 2026

Founder-led, unpolished video keeps beating produced ads on ROAS

Founder-led video reports an average 4.6x ROAS against 3.1x for product-focused ads in the same benchmark set, and inbound replies to founder-style posts convert at 14.6% versus 1.7% for outbound. The claim comes from a single content-marketing benchmark report, not an audited industry-wide study, flagged here as such.

Why it mattersThe gap is now large enough, even allowing for one report's bias, that who is talking is doing more conversion work than how well it is shot.

The historical bridge

1920s-1960s, United States

The advertising thermometer

Coca-Cola and thousands of local retailers gave away porcelain and tin advertising thermometers, hung in diners, gas stations and corner stores. The gimmick was not the brand name printed across the top, it was the mercury: a piece of paid media that changed its own message, the actual temperature, in real time, for free, decades before anyone called it dynamic creative. A hardware store thermometer told you the weather and reminded you where to buy a furnace filter in the same glance.

Why it still holds. Ace Hardware's weather triggered programmatic ads and Hoka's Strava powered OOH ticker are the same idea running on a different substrate, an ad unit that reacts to a live external signal instead of carrying one fixed message all month. The thermometer did it with mercury and a printing press, the digital screen does it with an API. The principle that outlasted the century is that an advertisement earns a second look by being useful and current, not just seen.
